"'''Mad About Me'''" was a song performed by [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes]]. One of their favorites, it was being played by them in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] entered to find passage off [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]. Kenobi and Skywalker got into a fight with the patrons [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]] and [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]] shortly after arriving, interrupting the playing of the Modal Nodes, but when the fracas died down, they resumed the song. The Modal Nodes performed it again in Chalmun's later that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], during a broadcast by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] about life on Tatooine. The bartender [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena's]] own song, "[[Goodnight, But Not Goodbye/Legends|Goodnight, But Not Goodbye]]," shared many elements of its instrumentals with "Mad About Me." Many years later, [[Reelo Baruk]]'s [[Baruk's Bar|bar]] on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] kept the song playing as ambient music.

==Performances==
"Mad About Me" was written at some point before [[3643 BBY]].<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> The [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Junk dealer/Legends|junk dealer]] [[Watto/Legends|Watto]] often hummed the tune to himself in his [[Wald's Parts|shop]] in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]], on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="racer">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']].</ref> By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], the song had become a favorite of the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] [[Jizz/Legends|jizz]] band [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes]].<ref name="CGG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=The Bith Shuffle}}</ref> The tune, though fairly nondescript, was bouncy,<ref name="HT">{{StoryCite|story=Hammertong: The Tale of the "Tonnika Sisters"|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> and the Modal Nodes' rendition of it was particularly upbeat.<ref name="EB" /> In 0 BBY, the Modal Nodes got a job as the regular band at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]].<ref name="WDDW">{{StoryCite|story=We Don't Do Weddings: The Band's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> On the day the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and his protege [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] came to Mos Eisley in search of transport off Tatooine, the band squabbled over their choice of song before choosing "Mad About Me."<ref name="EB" /> The band, however, was unaccustomed to performing at places like Chalmun's,<ref name="SO">{{StoryCite|story=Soup's On: The Pipe Smoker's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> and their performance of it was off both key and tempo, glaringly noticeable to patrons with sensitive hearing like the [[Chadra-Fan/Legends|Chadra-Fan]] [[Kabe/Legends|Kabe]].<ref name="PIA">{{StoryCite|story=Play It Again, Figrin D'an: The Tale of Muftak and Kabe|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> Shortly after their performance began, Kenobi and Skywalker arrived; upon entering, Skywalker was harassed by two of the patrons, [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]] and [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]]. As the situation turned violent, Kenobi brought out his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and cut off Baba's arm.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Where a band more experienced with the [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] would have continued to play in harmony with the chaos around them, the Modal Nodes promptly stopped,<ref name="SO" /> but when the fracas had died down they picked up where they had left off and finished the song.<ref name="ANH" />

Later that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], the Modal Nodes played a performance of "Mad About Me" for an interplanetary [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] broadcast about life on Tatooine. They were once again interrupted, as the Empire announced that it was imposing a curfew on the [[Tatoo system/Legends|Tatoo system]], effective immediately. The song that the bartender [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]] sang to encourage her customers to leave, "[[Goodnight, But Not Goodbye/Legends|Goodnight, But Not Goodbye]]," had instrumentals very similar to "Mad About Me," which were also played by the Modal Nodes.<ref name="HS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> The following year, "Mad About Me" received a good deal of play in cantinas across Tatooine.<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], a [[Baruk's Bar|bar]] on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] owned by [[Reelo Baruk]] had "Mad About Me" playing as ambient music.<ref name="JO">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Can you imagine several creatures in a future century finding some 1930s Benny Goodman swing band music in a time capsule or under a rock someplace&mdash;and how they might attempt to interpret it?|George Lucas|<ref name="SE soundtrack">[[Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope Original Soundtrack|''Star Wars: A New Hope Special Edition'' soundtrack]] liner notes</ref>}}
The cue titled "Cantina Band" was scored by [[John Williams]] for [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], released in [[1977]]. While it received its [[in-universe]] name, "Mad About Me," from the short story ''[[Empire Blues: The Devaronian's Tale]]'' in [[1995]]'s ''[[Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina]]'', it is titled "Cantina Band" on the film's many [[Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope Original Soundtrack|soundtracks]]. The piece is a rare example of source music in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' films&mdash;music that does not exist out of universe on the soundtrack, but is played diegetically by characters within the film. Alongside its corresponding piece "[[Dune Sea Special/Legends|Cantina Band #2]]," it is one of only two such cues to appear in ''A New Hope''.

Filmmaker [[George Lucas]] initially planned to use [[Wikipedia:Glenn Miller|Glenn Miller]] for the cantina sequence in ''A New Hope'', but the music cannot be used for his film. John Williams thus created something familiar, which Lucas described as "very Forties, yet very odd." While the music was originally designed as a big-band number, Lucas thought Williams's music worked well.<ref name="Rolling Stone">{{WebCite|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/movie-news/george-lucas-the-wizard-of-star-wars-2-232011|text=George Lucas: The Wizard of 'Star Wars'|author=Paul Scanlon|date=1977-08-25|archivedate=20200623204338}}</ref>

Lucas also proposed the inclusion of a [[Wikipedia:Jitterbug|jitterbug]]-like piece in the film, along the lines of the music of jazz musician [[Wikipedia:Benny Goodman|Benny Goodman]]. As his inspiration, Lucas had the idea of beings in the far future trying to create their own version of Goodman's style of music. John Williams wrote "Cantina Band" with this as his basis, scoring it so the instruments sounded somewhat strange, but on the verge of familiarity. To produce the piece, Williams brought in nine [[Wikipedia:Jazz|jazz]] musicians, a solo [[Wikipedia:Trumpet|trumpet]], two [[Wikipedia:Saxophone|saxophones]], a saxophonist who also played [[Wikipedia:Clarinet|clarinet]], a [[Wikipedia:Rhodes piano|Fender Rhodes piano]], a [[Wikipedia:Caribbean|Caribbean]] [[Wikipedia:Steel drum|steel drum]], another [[Wikipedia:Drum|drum]], various percussion instruments, and an [[Wikipedia:ARP Instruments, Inc.|ARP]] [[Wikipedia:Synthesizer|synthesizer]] for the bass. To give the instruments a more alien quality, the music was filtered so the bottom end of the sound was clipped, the lower end was attenuated, and a reverb was added to thin the instruments out.<ref name="SE soundtrack" /><ref name="Original soundtrack">[[Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope Original Soundtrack|''Star Wars'' Original Soundtrack]] liner notes</ref>

In 1977, [[Wikipedia:Disco|disco]] producer [[Wikipedia:Meco|Meco]] created an instrumental piece called "[[Wikipedia:Star Wars Theme/Cantina Band|Star Wars Theme/Cantina Band]]," which combined the [[Star Wars Main Title|main theme]] of the films with "Cantina Band" in a disco style. It was released on the album [[Wikipedia:Star Wars and Other Galactic Funk|''Star Wars and Other Galactic Funk'']], and on [[October 1]], 1977, it hit number one on the [[Wikipedia:Billboard Hot 100|Billboard Hot 100]], where it remained for two weeks.<ref name="Billboard">{{BookCite|author=Bronson, Fred|title=The Billboard Book of Number One Hits|publisher=Billboard Books|date=2003|isbn=9780823076772}}</ref>

Like many ''Star Wars'' cues, "Cantina Band" has been used in a number of [[Star Wars video games|video game]]s&mdash;often as part of the soundtrack, as opposed to source music. In ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', it appears as part of a medley of unusual ''Star Wars'' tracks played during the "Assault" mode of the Mos Eisley level of the game's Instant Action feature. ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'' plays it on some levels when the player uses [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] on chairs, and its sequel ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'' uses "Cantina Band" as the background music in the Mos Eisley cantina. The short film ''[[LEGO Star Wars: Revenge of the Brick]]'' plays it during a cantina scene of its own, reminiscent of the one in ''A New Hope''. ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'' plays the piece over its opening [[LucasArts]] logo, while dozens of dancing [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] form the logo.

A short variation of the song, played in a quieter classical style, can be heard as part of the music played in and around the [[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']] attraction at Disney theme parks.

The cue has made several appearances as source music, too. In ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]'', it is heard in a bar on Nar Shaddaa. This was a first for the [[Dark Forces/Jedi Knight|''Jedi Knight'' series]], as earlier games ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]'' use the relatively rarer "Cantina Band #2" as their source music. ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' features both; the two "Cantina Band" pieces play on an infinite loop in all cantinas on Tatooine. Additionally, a variation of "Cantina Band," known as "Starwars2" in-game, is included as one of the playable songs of the "Entertainer" player class. In ''[[Star Wars: Yoda Stories]]'', a brief portion of the song is played whenever the player enters any cantina on any planet. ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'' and its [[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption|expansion pack]] play the song as ambient music when the game's camera is moved near a cantina structure on land maps. ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'' uses the song in its cantina scene as well; it additionally introduces a version of the piece with lyrics, titled "Goodnight, But Not Goodbye" and sung by [[Bea Arthur]]. In the [[Star Wars home video releases|DVD releases]] of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] and the original trilogy, the song is used as background music for an [[Easter egg (virtual)|Easter egg]] which plays a blooper reel along with DVD credits.
